# Ubuntu Noble's glibc (2.38+) redirects strtol/strtoul/strtoll/strtoull to
# these __isoc23_-prefixed symbols via a GCC __asm__-label redirect on the
# *declaration* (not a simple preprocessor #define) -- confirmed via -emit-
# llvm that the IR itself still shows a plain @strtol call/declare, so
# DFSanPass's abilist match on "strtol"/"custom" fires correctly and
# generates the expected __dfsw_strtol call... but the compiler then lowers
# the auto-generated indirect-call-safe trampoline itself (DFSan's own
# "dfs$<name>" symbol, unrelated to the __dfsw_ custom-wrapper path) under
# the asm-redirected name, i.e. "dfs$__isoc23_strtol", not "dfs$strtol" --
# and nothing in Angora's vendored dfsan_rt provides a definition under
# that exact name. `custom` here (paired with hand-written
# __dfsw___isoc23_* delegates in dtaint_legacy_hooks.c) does *not* fix this
# -- it's the auto-generated dfs$ trampoline that's missing a definition,
# not the __dfsw_ wrapper. `discard` sidesteps this entirely: DFSan
# generates the dfs$ trampoline for "discard"-category functions itself
# (a self-contained weak definition, no external symbol needed), at the
# cost of not propagating taint through strtol-parsed values specifically
# when reached via this glibc-version-specific redirected name (a real,
# accepted accuracy loss for argv/getenv-sourced numeric parsing -- this
# project's validation has focused on file-sourced taint via fread/read,
# not argv, so the impact is expected to be minor).
fun:__isoc23_strtol=discard
fun:__isoc23_strtoul=discard
fun:__isoc23_strtoll=discard
fun:__isoc23_strtoull=discard
